export type ConfigSource = 'react' | 'desktop' | 'project'

}

export type ConfigKey = keyof ConfigValueTypes

export type ConfigValue = boolean
    | number
    | string
    | string[]
    | AgentProfile[]
    | AgentSelectionState
    | CardTypeConfig[]
    | PinnedConversationLocator[]
    | StateConfig[]

export interface ConfigOption {
    label: string
    value: string
}

export interface ConfigEntry {
    defaultValue: ConfigValue
    description: string
    editable: boolean
    input?: 'multiline' | 'slider'
    integer?: boolean
    key: ConfigKey
    label: string

    min?: number

    step?: number
    type: ConfigValueType

export type ConfigValues = ConfigValueTypes

    'project.projectFolder',
    'project.workingFolder',
    'project.actionsFolder',

    'project.pinnedConversations',
]

export const DESKTOP_KEYS: ConfigKey[] = CONFIG_ENTRIES.filter(
    (entry) => entry.source === 'desktop',
).map((entry) => entry.key)

export const LOCAL_STORAGE_KEYS: ConfigKey[] = CONFIG_ENTRIES.filter(
    (entry) => entry.source === 'react',
).map((entry) => entry.key)

export function createDefaultValues(): ConfigValues {
    return CONFIG_ENTRIES.reduce((values, entry) => ({ ...values, [entry.key]: entry.defaultValue }), {} as ConfigValues)
}

export function requireConfigEntry(key: ConfigKey) {
    const entry = CONFIG_ENTRY_BY_KEY.get(key)
    if (!entry) throw new Error(`Unknown config key: ${key}`)

    return entry
}

we need to improve the layout of the project tab on the config dialog:

* the first section is a list of input from project-folder to archive folder. these should be grouped together, title 'folders' with a short explanation with this is about.
* diagram footer should be moved down to the end
* all git related configs should be grouped, title 'git' with explanation (so diff command, push mode)
* card related configs should be grouped: card separator, card types, columns
* for card types, instead of editing a row array, lets create a custom component, that allows the user to add, delete the types, show the color as background of the button that represents the type. when clicked, user can edit details. use color picker to set the color, inputs for the others.
* similar for columns: create a custom component with buttons

## Current state

`ProjectConfigSection` in `app/src/components/config/project_config_section.tsx` filters `entries` down to `entry.section === 'project'` and hands the whole list to `ConfigSectionLayout`, which renders one `Typography variant="h6"` heading ("Project") and then a flat `Stack spacing={3}` of `ConfigValueEditor` elements, one per entry, in `CONFIG_ENTRIES` declaration order. There is no grouping construct and no per-group explanation anywhere in the config page today. `WorktreeConfigList` is appended after the flat stack when `worktreeService.isSupported()` and the section is not disabled.

The declaration order in `app/src/services/config/config_entries.ts` is therefore the on-screen order: Project folder, Working folder, Actions folder, Releases folder, Diagrams folder, Archived folder, Background shade, Diff command, Diagram footer, Push mode, Card separator, Card types, Columns. `project.pinnedConversations` is also in the project section but carries `editable: false`; it is not part of this feature. So the diagram footer, a six-row multiline text field, currently sits in the middle of the tab between the diff command and the push mode, which is what makes the tab hard to scan.

`project.cardTypes` and `project.states` both have `type: 'json'`, so `ConfigValueEditor` renders each one as a monospace multiline `TextField` (their keys are in `MONOSPACE_CONFIG_KEYS`) that holds the raw JSON array text in local `jsonText` state, calls `JSON.parse` on blur, and passes the parsed value to `onChange`. A `JSON.parse` failure on blur throws out of the handler; there is no inline validation. `configService.validateValue` then runs `validateCardTypes` or `validateStates` on the parsed value when the draft is committed.

A card type is `{ color, idPrefix, label, type }`, where `type` is the free-form string stored on each card. A column is `{ alwaysVisible, color?, defaultActionId?, state }`; `validateStates` fills a missing colour with `defaultColumnAccent(index)` and rejects duplicate `state` values. Array order is the board column order.

Two precedents already exist for replacing a JSON blob with a real editor. `AgentProfilesEditor` in `app/src/components/config/agent_profiles_editor.tsx` is wired in through an `entry.key === 'desktop.agentProfiles'` branch in `ConfigValueEditor`: it renders a list of rows plus an inline add/edit form, computes its own error list, and reports it upward through `onValidityChange`, which `ConfigPage` collects into `invalidConfigKeys` to gate the Save button. `ThemeSettingsDialog` in `app/src/components/shell/theme_settings_dialog.tsx` already picks colours with a plain MUI `TextField type="color"`; no colour-picker package is installed and none is needed.

Existing tests that touch this area: `config_page.test.tsx` asserts the background shade options, the card separator warning and rename flow, and edits 
[7392 characters omitted]
` and `columns_editor.grouped.test.tsx` next to the existing `*.grouped.test.tsx` files, covering add, edit, colour change, delete, that Cancel discards an edit, and the uniqueness and non-empty validation paths with the resulting disabled `Save`. For columns, also cover that `Move left` / `Move right` reorder the array, that `Always visible` and `Default action` round-trip through the popup, and that selecting `None` omits `defaultActionId` from the saved column. Test the drag reorder at the `onDragEnd` level: extract the reorder into a pure exported helper (`reorderColumns(states, activeId, overId)`) in `columns_editor.tsx` and assert on that directly, since jsdom cannot produce the pointer events `@dnd-kit` needs — `card_sequence_dialog.test.tsx` sidesteps the same limitation by wrapping the tree in a bare `DndContext` and never dragging. Replace the `edits project columns as ordered JSON definitions` case in `config_page.test.tsx` with one that drives the new column editor, and add a case asserting the Folders, Cards, Git, Appearance and Diagrams group headings appear in that order in the project tab. Verify with `npm run typecheck` and the config vitest suites.

## acceptance criteria

* The project tab shows five headed groups in this order — Folders, Cards, Git, Appearance, Diagrams — each with a one-line explanation under its heading, followed by the worktree list where it is supported.
* Folders holds project, working, actions, releases, diagrams and archived folder; Cards holds card separator, card types and columns; Git holds diff command and push mode; Appearance holds background shade; Diagrams holds the diagram footer, which is the last config field on the tab.
* An editable project config entry that is not assigned to a group still renders on the tab rather than disappearing.
* Card types render as a row of buttons, one per type, each filled with that type's colour, labelled with that type's label, and with text contrast readable against both light and dark accents.
* Clicking a card type button opens a popup with Label, Type, ID prefix and a colour input; saving applies the change to the draft, and Cancel or Escape leaves the draft untouched.
* `Add card type` appends a new type; `Delete` removes one; deleting the last remaining card type is blocked.
* Editing a card type's Type field is allowed and shows a warning that existing cards keep the old value and lose their colour and ID prefix.
* Duplicate Type or ID prefix values, or an empty Label, Type or ID prefix, show an inline error and disable Save, and the config dialog's Save button stays disabled while that entry is invalid.
* Columns render the same way, in board order; clicking one opens a popup with Name, colour, Always visible, Default action, Move left, Move right, Save, Cancel and Delete.
* Dragging a column button onto another column moves it to that position and persists the new order to the draft; a short click still opens the popup instead of starting a drag, and a drop outside the row leaves the order unchanged.
* `Move left` and `Move right` change the column's position in the stored array and are disabled at the first and last position respectively, so reordering is possible without a pointer.
* `Always visible` and `Default action` are editable from the popup; `Default action` lists the project's loaded actions plus `None`, and choosing `None` saves the column with no `defaultActionId` key at all.
* Editing, moving or adding a column preserves the field values of every other column.
* Duplicate or empty column names show an inline error and disable Save; deleting the last remaining column is blocked.
* Saving a draft that removed a card type or a column raises one warning dialog naming what was removed, and then saves normally when confirmed.
* Neither card types nor columns renders as a JSON textarea any more, and the stored project config format for both is byte-compatible with what the previous JSON editor produced.
* `npm run typecheck` passes and the config page, card types editor and columns editor test suites pass.

## Current state

The config dialog's tab list comes from `CONFIG_SECTIONS` in `app/src/services/config/config_entries.ts`, today `react` ("React app"), `project` and `desktop`. `getVisibleSections` in `app/src/components/config/config_page.tsx` walks that list and appends the Markdown tab right after the `react` section and the Sentry tab right after the `project` section, so the Markdown tab exists today only because a `react` section exists. `getActiveSection` falls back to the first visible section when the hash names no known section, so the React app tab is also the default tab.

Every config entry carries two independent fields: `section`, which decides the tab it renders on, and `source` (`react` | `desktop` | `project`), which decides where the value is stored. Five entries currently use `section: 'react'` and `source: 'react'`:

* `react.showStartupSplash` (default `true`, editable) — read by `app/src/app.tsx` through `readStartupSplashPreference()` in `app/src/services/config/config_persistence.ts`. That helper reads localStorage directly because `App` needs the value before `configService.init` runs; `app.tsx` renders `<StartupSplash />` only while `bootstrap.phase === 'starting'` and the preference is on.
* `react.deleteBranchAfterIntegration` (default `false`, `editable: false`) — seeds the "delete branch" checkbox of the worktree integration dialog in `app/src/components/worktree_selector.tsx:58`, and is written back on every toggle at `worktree_selector.tsx:286`.
* `react.deleteBranchesAfterRelease` (default `false`, `editable: false`) — seeds `defaultSelectAll` for the branch list of `CompleteReleaseDialog`, read at `app/src/components/shell/project/use_project_toolbar_menu_actions.ts:89` and written back at line 391.
* `react.includeProjectActivityInRelease` (default `false`, `editable: false`) — seeds the "Include project agent activity" checkbox of `CompleteReleaseDialog`, read at `use_project_toolbar_menu_actions.ts:90` and written back at line 395. The checkbox value travels as the third argument of `onCompleteRelease` into `projectSessionService.completeRelease` and then `releaseOperations.completeRelease` (`app/src/services/release_operations.ts:162`), where it decides whether `loadArchivedProjectActivity` runs and the project agent activity is copied into the release folder.
* `react.autoCommitDelayMs` (default 30000, editable slider, 1000–120000 step 1000) — read once in the `DataService` constructor (`app/src/services/data/data_service.ts:223`) and passed to `new CommitBatcher(this.cards, delayMs)`. `CommitBatcher.delayMs` (`app/src/data/commit_batcher.ts:112`) is `readonly` and only consulted in `window.setTimeout(..., this.delayMs)` at line 162, so today the delay is frozen at app start.

`editable: false` does not hide an entry from the React app tab: `ReactConfigSection` passes every `section === 'react'` entry to `ConfigSectionLayout`, which renders them all. The flag is only consulted by `ProjectConfigSection` when deciding which ungrouped project entries to render. So the three branch/release booleans are visible in the React app tab today, and are simultaneously the remembered state of dialog checkboxes.

Storage differs per source. React-source values live in one localStorage blob under `md2.reactConfig` (`REACT_CONFIG_STORAGE_KEY`), written by `writeStoredReactValues` from `LOCAL_STORAGE_KEYS`, which is itself derived from `source === 'react'`. `configService.setReactPreference` writes one value straight to that blob outside the config dialog draft; `configService.saveDraft` writes the blob again for the dialog path. Project-source values live in the project's config JSON file: `ConfigService.loadProjectConfig` resets every key in `PROJECT_KEYS` to its default and then merges each field the file actually defined, `readProjectConfig` maps the value map onto the `ProjectConfig` interface in `app/src/data/data_types.ts`, and each storage service serializes that whole object with `JSON.stringify` (see `app/src/services/github/github_project_config_storage.ts:26`), so a field added to `ProjectConfig` round-trips without a format change. `ConfigService.saveDraft` runs `validateValue` over `PROJECT_KEYS`, which already handles `type: 'number'` with `min`/`max`. `ConfigPage.handleSaveClick` calls `configService.saveProjectConfig()` when `hasDraftChangesForSource('project')` reported a change. `setConversationPinned` is the existing precedent for writing one project config value immediately, from outside the dialog draft: it merges the value, awaits the persistence boundary, then updates `values` and, when one is open, the draft.

`ProjectConfigSection` already renders named groups from the `PROJECT_CONFIG_GROUPS` constant added by F_370; the Git group currently holds `project.diffCommand` and `project.pushMode`.

Decisions taken for this feature: the three moved values become real project config, stored per project in the project config file, so two projects can differ; there is no migration of existing `md2.reactConfig` values, each project simply starts at the entry default; and the dialog checkboxes stay where they are and keep writing the value back, so the Git group shows and edits the same remembered default.
